decisions.evidence: Both long revisions have severely garbled opening chronology and payment clauses; neither is a clearly valid monologue despite revision 1's improved later wording.
Fail followed by could have chosen victory forms the most coherent admonition, but save us all/save her and shared/chosen are audible semantic alternatives.
Who among them can stop us? is a grammatical rhetorical killing-streak boast; Two among them reverses the intended meaning.
'Em and them are distinct audible forms and both produce the same coherent Abrams boast.
Both component revisions are nonsensical and do not express Abrams's area-immobilize ability use.
Seven's in mid and the elliptical Seven in mid are both natural tactical pings; apostrophe-s cannot be inferred.
Going to shop directly matches the self-reported going-shop filename; Go into shop is an imperative with different meaning.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Lash; Clash/Klash are phonetic errors.
I see Calico is the sighting callout indicated by the filename; seek changes the action.
Every component revision says Chat/Shift instead of authoritative Shiv, so none expresses the mid-location ping.
Shun/Sun Wrecker do not express the Stun Wrecker command required by the filename.
Heys/he's fail to identify authoritative Haze in the was-here ping.

Neither Heys nor Hey identifies Haze as required by the get-back filename.

Both revisions omit Lash and convert the filename's report about Lash into a different first-person group suggestion.

Neither revision names Viscous or forms the on-top-of-mid sighting ping indicated by the filename.
We learned and we've learned are distinct tense/contraction forms and both complete the loss-line wordplay.
The trailing Mmm is an audible vocalization and cannot be added or removed based on upgrade context.

Can collect the spirits, collect spirits, and can collect spirits differ in audible modal/article words and are all coherent objective calls.
